initial_findings: All main numerical exercises already had correct answers; the lesson was not missing an entire core chapter topic.
Specificity, the listening-history application, the zero-probability independence exception, and an explicit countably infinite Bayes statement were missing or implicit.
The gambler’s-ruin telescoping derivation was compressed; the Pólya aside gave warnings but did not state the actual theorem.
The slides use sensitivity 0.96 in the question and 0.95 in a later substitution; the existing lesson correctly used 0.96.
The source’s unrestricted claim that two synchronous random walkers are guaranteed to meet is false without movement/parity assumptions.
changes: Added or expanded source applications, specificity, symmetric/zero-case independence, full chain-rule conditions, and countable Bayes cases.
Expanded independence exercises with complement and route reasoning.
Added full geometric-increment/telescoping gambler’s-ruin derivation, model domain, fair-case limit explanation and absorption argument.
Replaced the vague random-walk aside with a precise theorem, academic source, parity counterexample and a 1D connection to the ruin formula.
remaining_limitations: The full proof of Pólya’s 2D recurrence theorem is not in the slides and is not developed here; the theorem and its assumptions are explained.
The sports percentages are treated as hypothetical inputs from the slides, not verified historical statistics.
